title: Fleet Control Center: quick-scaling actions, throughput heatmap, and audit timeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity need a single place in Console to make operational scaling decisions quickly and safely. Current console surfaces are fragmented: scaling presets live in one page, throughput charts in another, and audit logs are hard to correlate with scale events. That fragmentation slows incident response and makes it hard to reason about cost/throughput trade-offs.

Goal: Ship a Fleet Control Center panel that groups quick-scaling actions (scale-to, step-scale, schedule window), an interactive throughput heatmap and timeline (per-pool, per-model), and a compact audit/change timeline that surfaces who changed what and why. The panel should also provide a lightweight cost-preview for scale changes and surface guardrails (RBAC, soft-limits, canary policies).

Scope:
- Quick-actions toolbar: scale-to-target, step-scale (+/- N GPUs), pin-to-min, cancel active scaling operations, and a "simulate impact" preview.
- Throughput heatmap: 1h/6h/24h/7d/30d rollups, model and pool filters, median P95 latency overlay, and a selectable timeframe for the audit timeline.
- Audit timeline: ordered, human-readable entries for configuration changes and autoscale events; diffs between versions; exportable CSV; linkbacks to PR/incident.
- Cost preview: approximate delta per-hour and per-month before applying changes (uses current cost model in Optimize).
- Safeguards: RBAC checks (only fleet-admins or owners can force scale), confirmation modal with recovery steps, and optional canary rollout policy selector.

Out of scope for this ticket: full runbook automation, capacity rebalancing logic, and per-customer SLA configuration UI (handled by PM-16602).
acceptance_criteria: Quick-actions are visible in the Fleet Control Center for pools where the current user has fleet-control permissions
Scale-to and step-scale requests call the new Fleet Control API (ENG-5120) and return immediate UI feedback (success/error)
Throughput heatmap shows aggregated throughput and P95 latency for selected pool/model for 7d and 30d ranges
Audit timeline records all manual scale actions and scheduled windows with user, timestamp, and delta; entries link to the exact change payload
Cost preview displays estimated per-hour delta and warns when estimated monthly delta > 15% of current spend
RBAC prevents non-admins from using force-scale; confirmation modal is shown for any change that increases capacity by >= 50%
Unit and integration tests cover telemetry events emitted for scaling actions and audit entries
Design sign-off obtained (DES-1182) and backend API contract approved by ENG (ENG-5120)
notes: Trade-offs: running detailed cost simulations client-side is expensive; we will use a server-side estimate endpoint that returns a small set of buckets (low/median/high) to keep UI latency under 300ms.
Telemetry: every quick-action must emit event 'fleet.control.action' with {action,type,old_capacity,new_capacity,initiator,simulation} for billing and postmortem analyses.
Data retention: audit timeline entries for scaling should be retained for 365 days by default; longer retention will be an add-on (opt-in).
Rollout: start with 20% of orgs on Dedicated in staging, then 100% on staging for two weeks, then gradual rollout to prod with feature flag.
